headline: High-risk shared-server orchestration: Langflow can write and execute server-side code while LlamaFactory is non-interactive, making prompt injection and data leakage plausible but not catastrophic by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain agents server-side, so attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions if a flow reads it. LlamaFactory has no filesystem or network surfaces, so it is not itself an injection source; the pair risk comes from Langflow’s permissive flow wiring rather than any bidirectional channel.
conditions: IF a Langflow flow reads untrusted uploaded content as prompt text, injection becomes reachable.
IF LlamaFactory remains non-interactive with no file or network outputs, it does not amplify injection.
mitigations: Add a strict prompt/content separator in Langflow flows.
Disable or review any node that parses uploaded text as instructions.
Use allowlisted templates for any agent-to-agent handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
Run a one-time audit of flows that consume user files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, server filesystem, and stored credentials, while LlamaFactory exposes no file or network egress. The pair can still leak sensitive flow data if Langflow writes it to shared server state or files that other processes can read; the blast radius is multiple work products, not just one document.
conditions: IF Langflow stores intermediate outputs on a shared server filesystem, leakage is reachable.
IF LlamaFactory is granted filesystem access outside its current profile, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict Langflow storage to per-flow isolated directories.
Purge intermediate outputs after each run.
Review secrets stored in Langflow’s component store.
Confirm LlamaFactory remains fileless and offline.
requires-engineering: encrypt shared server-side state at rest.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad shell, subprocess, and filesystem write capability, but LlamaFactory has no write, shell, or network capabilities, so there is little direct resource contention. The pair only conflicts if an external orchestrator gives LlamaFactory mutable access not shown in its profile; that uncertainty would raise severity, but the current profiles do not show it.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is later granted write or shell access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state not present in the profiles, contention becomes reachable.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only.
Separate working directories per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes from Langflow flows.
requires-engineering: add file locks if shared state is introduced.
Document any future mutable scopes before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream nodes. LlamaFactory is not runnable and has no action-taking surfaces, which limits harm, but if Langflow feeds its outputs into another flow step without verification, errors can cascade across work products.
conditions: IF a Langflow node consumes prior node output without validation, cascading error is reachable.
IF LlamaFactory is used only as a static reference artifact, cascade risk stays low.
mitigations: Insert validation nodes between Langflow steps.
Require schema checks on all model outputs.
Mark unverified outputs as non-authoritative in flow templates.
requires-engineering: add automated regression tests for critical flows.
Limit downstream actions to read-only operations.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. Langflow handles flow inputs and stored credentials, while LlamaFactory touches no data classes, so compliance risk is limited to deployment-specific handling rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF Langflow is deployed with regulated data and retention is not configured, compliance risk increases.
IF LlamaFactory is later connected to regulated data stores, a mismatch may emerge.
mitigations: Review Langflow retention settings.
Avoid storing regulated data in flow inputs.
Confirm secrets handling policy for Langflow store.
Document data residency for any shared deployment.
requires-engineering: add compliance controls to deployment manifests.
